title: The Doppler Effect
text: The Doppler effect is the change in frequency or wavelength of a wave relative to an observer who is moving relative to the wave source. For sound waves, the Doppler effect causes the pitch of a sound to appear higher as the source approaches and lower as it moves away. Austrian physicist Christian Doppler described this effect in 1842. The effect applies to all wave phenomena, including light and other electromagnetic radiation. In astronomy, the Doppler shift of light from distant galaxies provides evidence for the expansion of the universe — galaxies moving away from Earth show a redshift, where their light is shifted toward longer, redder wavelengths.
